newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss agree to join NATO's Partnership scheme.
newsitem.headline: Swiss agree to join NATO's Partnership scheme.

text.p: Switzerland said on Wednesday it had formally decided to join NATO's Partnership for Peace programme in a bid to promote security in post-Cold War Europe.

"The cabinet authorised the foreign minister to sign framework documents for the partnership," a government statement said, adding the step did not compromise Swiss neutrality or signal its intention to join the Western military alliance.
"The federal council (cabinet) wants to make clear that participating in PFP does not create any obligations under international law and does not affect neutrality," the statement said.
"The federal council wants to make clear that Switzerland is neutral and does not want to enter NATO."

NATO -- the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation -- launched the PFP scheme in 1994 to help foster ties with its former East Bloc adversaries who had embraced democracy after the collapse of communism in Eastern Europe.
Ther are now 27 partner countries, including other neutrals Finland, Austria and Sweden.
